Hi Sara — thanks for the note and the timeline. Apologies for the initial lag; happy to consolidate artifacts. High-level answers up front, details below and files attached.

Short answers:
- Diagram: attached PNG is an annotated topology covering Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes and the isolation model we apply for Dedicated and Private customers.
- Cross-tenant egress: Redwood enforces per-tenant egress policies via dedicated VPC peering/Private deployment routing controls and platform-enforced SNAT gating for Hosted. For Dedicated we bind tenant traffic to reserved GPU pools and dedicated egress subnets — see the isolation matrix sheet for per-mode controls.
- KMS boundaries: Customers who choose Private or Dedicated with KMS integration keep keys in their own cloud KMS (customer-managed). For Hosted accounts we support BYOK through customer KMS integration; at-rest keys for platform-managed stores are envelope-encrypted and rotated per our key rotation policy. See the KMS statement doc for exact wording (attached on request).

Expanded notes (for auditor):
1) Topology (attached): the diagram shows control plane (Redwood-managed) separated from data plane instances. In Dedicated mode the data plane sits in a customer-dedicated subnet overlay with no shared tenant data-plane compute. Network ACLs and security groups enforce minimal inbound flows (control-plane telemetry only) and egress is restricted to approved customer destinations. In Private (VPC) we deploy the control plane connectors into the customer's VPC, and the inference hosts live behind customer-managed routing policies (air-gapped option documented).

2) Egress controls: per-tenant egress enforcement is done at two layers: (a) deployment-time network policies (VPC-level routing + firewall rules), (b) runtime enforcement in the serving runtime that blocks outbound sockets not in allowed lists for the tenant. The isolation-matrix sheet enumerates allowed outbound ports and destinations per offering and includes example firewall rules and NAT config.

3) KMS and key handling: For Dedicated & Private, customers can provide KMS keys (cloud KMS or HSM) and we never persist plaintext keys on platforms. The platform uses envelope encryption: model cache and ephemeral KV caches are encrypted with data-plane keys which are themselves wrapped by customer keys where provided. For Hosted accounts that do not supply keys, we use our platform-managed key store and provide rotation and audit logs.

4) Evidence & artifacts: attached diagram + matrix. If you need a CAIQ/SIG-ready narrative (short text blocks mapped to specific control IDs), we can produce a mapping file that ties each topology statement to SIG/CAT questions. I can produce that mapping within 48 hours.

Next steps: Sara, tell us which of these you want first (diagram + KMS statement now, or full mapping to SIG controls). If the auditor needs an Azure/AWS-specific breakout, call that out and we will generate cloud-specific ACL examples.

Best,

Sara & Ben — quick update and clarifications per auditor follow-up questions: 

A) Customer-managed KMS: for Dedicated and Private we support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). When enabled, the customer key policy binds key usage to the data-plane instances in their tenancy and Redwood holds no ability to decrypt key material without explicit key access granted in the customer's cloud account. This is documented in the attached kms-boundary-statement.pdf.

B) Controlled egress examples: auditor asked for an example rule set — from the isolation-matrix sheet, example NAT and security group entries are: deny all outbound by default; allow 443 to customer-approved destinations; allow telemetry to control-plane endpoints on port 443 with mTLS. We also include a runtime check that rejects any outbound DNS resolution that doesn't match allowed domains.

C) Evidence tie-in to SIG: we will produce a short CSV mapping SIG question ids to the paragraph numbers in the attached diagram + matrix. We will scope to the network and key management family (approximately 18 control questions).

Delivery commitment: I will post the SIG mapping file and a one-page attestation by end-of-day 12/18 PST. If you need earlier, tell me which three controls are highest priority and I will prioritize them.

Regards,
